answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Proof of unique bridge crossing transponder, crossings logged on one bridge for five years becomes the price of admission, and the pearl is that the price is charged per identity. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that crossings logged on one bridge for five years — so privacy survives, and the ledge is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the karst is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
